title: Maintainer feedback (2026-11-03): sitting idle in the world on the hosted realm, the session dropped. The server log reads "closed by the server: a frame not read or written within 2 s" (twice, 18:51 and 18:52 UTC): network.rs read() bounds the wait for the NEXT frame by the same 2 s DEADLINE as completing one, so any 2 s gap in the client stream (a Wi-Fi or tunnel hiccup; the client pings each 1 s and sends 20 Hz moves) ends the session. Split it: keep 2 s for a frame once its length prefix has arrived and for writes, and bound the wait between frames by a longer idle limit that fits the edge (spec 12: pings 30 s, idle close 75 s), as an env var with a spec 01/02 default; log the gap that ended a session. Add a test that a 5 s gap between frames survives and a stalled half-frame still closes in 2 s.
testme: After the next deploy, sit idle in the world and on the select and create screens of the hosted realm for several minutes on Wi-Fi: the session stays up. Any server close line now reads 'no frame begun for 30 s, the connection idle limit' or 'a frame begun but not completed within 2 s (N of its M bytes)', not 'a frame not read or written within 2 s'.
